mutations.label: the gateway delete stops asking whether a connection still rides it, and a connected gateway vanishes under its private network (#282)
the backend delete stops asking whether a frontend still forwards to it, and the wrong destroy order silently succeeds
a detach stops releasing the address the attach booked, and the private network's pool leaks one address per balancer lifecycle

note: The two delete guards are the family the ownership audits singled out: creation paths are checked by habit, destruction paths are the ones that destroy. Terraform never triggers either refusal — it destroys children first — so nothing in the conformance suite would notice their removal; only these tests bite. The third mutation is the leak the shared IPAM pool makes expensive: the attach books a real address out of the same allocator the NICs draw from, and a detach that forgets it strands the address for every later NIC and booking.
